Safety screen: the chat log contains two messages only, both timestamped [F5]. At 18:24 the driver wrote "Please do not smoke in the car." [F3]; at the same minute the rider replied "Say that again and I will punch you." [F4]. Read in context, a punch is threatened against the driver personally, conditional on the driver repeating a lawful, non-confrontational in-car request — this is a threat of physical violence aimed at the other party, not mere rudeness in a route argument. The driver's post-trip statement says the same thing and adds that he kept driving and did not answer [F6]. On those words I record safety_concern = suspected, basis F3, F4, F6, and under SAFE-1 the case receives no automated ruling; it goes to a person with this summary.

The threat is not in dispute: both briefs concede it (C1/D1, D2/C2) and the log is complete and timestamped [F5], so the human reviewer is not asked to choose between competing versions of the chat — only to assess the words in F4 and any context the rider supplies that is not in this record. The rider's version beyond F4 is absent; SAFE-1 leaves that semantic assessment to the court reading the text, which is the reason this cannot be executed automatically.

No record needed by the applicable clause is missing, so evidence_status = sufficient and no gap is named.

RIDER: Your dispute on trip B-0045 has been passed to a Ryde reviewer. No decision has been made yet: nothing has been refunded or charged as part of this review. The reviewer will look at the messages exchanged and both parties' accounts of what happened. Ryde will contact you once the review is complete.

DRIVER: The dispute on trip B-0045 has been passed to a Ryde reviewer. No decision has been made yet, and nothing changes on your account or earnings as part of this review. The reviewer will look at the messages exchanged and both parties' accounts of what happened. Ryde will contact you once the review is complete.

ruling.recommended_action: Send the file to a Ryde human reviewer with the fact summary below; hold all automated fare decisions pending review; no account flag is raised on this record.
ruling.reasoning:
Safety screen: the chat log contains two messages only, both timestamped [F5]. At 18:24 the driver wrote "Please do not smoke in the car." [F3]; at the same minute the rider replied "Say that again and I will punch you." [F4]. Read in context, a punch is threatened against the driver personally, conditional on the driver repeating a lawful, non-confrontational in-car request — this is a threat of physical violence aimed at the other party, not mere rudeness in a route argument. The driver's post-trip statement says the same thing and adds that he kept driving and did not answer [F6]. On those words I record safety_concern = suspected, basis F3, F4, F6, and under SAFE-1 the case receives no automated ruling; it goes to a person with this summary.

The threat is not in dispute: both briefs concede it (C1/D1, D2/C2) and the log is complete and timestamped [F5], so the human reviewer is not asked to choose between competing versions of the chat — only to assess the words in F4 and any context the rider supplies that is not in this record. The rider's version beyond F4 is absent; SAFE-1 leaves that semantic assessment to the court reading the text, which is the reason this cannot be executed automatically.

Scope of the summary for the reviewer: what happened — 18:24 exchange (F3 then F4) during a RydeTAXI trip Tampines Mall → Changi Airport T3, pickup 18:15, drop-off 18:28, metered fare $20.75; the disputed item is the rider's F4 message; what to check — the rider's account of tone/context, whether earlier messages exist outside the two captured in F5; the driver reported no physical contact and no repetition of the threat [F6]. Note the report path: emergency medical help 995, driver's commercial motor insurance for injury claims, and reporting through RydeHELP (SAFE-2 informational context only — no accident, injury or dangerous-driving allegation appears in this file).

Fare/route elements are settled and raise nothing to refund: the GPS record shows actual 8.5 km against an optimal 8.5 km, i.e. +0.0 km and no off-route segment [F1], and 13.2 min against a 16.3 min estimate [F2]; with no off-route segment there is no unexempted segment under RD-1 and no refund computation under RD-2. No amount is stated because escalate carries no amount. A driver-filed safety case produces no account flag on these facts: the profiles (rider 735 d, 4.5, 0 disputes/0 upheld [F7]; driver 1974 d, 4.82, 743 trips, 0 disputes/0 upheld [F8]) are not the basis of any finding and no RD-6 condition (refund > 0 or recorded RD-1 breach) is met.

Evidence: the record settles what this ruling needs — a complete, fully timestamped chat record [F5] capturing the disputed message [F4] and the driver's corroborating statement [F6]; the route and duration figures are measured [F1][F2]. No record needed by the applicable clause is missing, so evidence_status = sufficient and no gap is named.

rejected_claims.reason: The driver's clean profile (1974 d, 4.82, 743 trips, 0 disputes, 0 upheld) is offered to support the credibility of his report; profile facts cannot decide a case alone and do not make the F4 words more or less threatening, so this claim carries no weight in the finding under SAFE-1 [F8].

The rider's profile (735 d, 4.5, 0 disputes, 0 upheld in 90 d) is offered to rebut any misconduct finding; profile facts cannot decide the case and no RD-6 condition (refund > 0 or recorded RD-1 breach) is met, so no account action follows here and the profile point does not affect the outcome [F7][RD-6].

ruling.escalation_reason: Driver-filed safety complaint: rider's timestamped chat message "Say that again and I will punch you." [F4], sent 18:24 in reply to the driver's 18:24 request not to smoke [F3], corroborated by the driver's statement [F6]. SAFE-1 bars an automatic ruling; human review of both accounts is required. No route/fare item exists to rule on [F1][F2].

actions.detail: Driver-filed safety complaint: rider's timestamped chat message "Say that again and I will punch you." [F4], sent 18:24 in reply to the driver's 18:24 request not to smoke [F3], corroborated by the driver's statement [F6]. SAFE-1 bars an automatic ruling; human review of both accounts is required. claims.assertion: This case is a driver-filed safety complaint in which the rider's own chat message is a threat of violence: F4 records the rider writing at 18:24, in response to the driver's request not to smoke (F3, 18:24), 'Say that again and I will punch you.' That is intimidation of the driver, and the chat record containing it is complete and fully timestamped (F5), so the message is not an artefact of a partial log.

The driver's written statement is consistent with and adds nothing contradicted by the record: F6 says he asked politely, the rider said he would punch him if he said it again, and he kept driving without answering; the only chat exchange (F3, F4) matches that account, so there is no factual dispute to resolve about what was said.

Because the threat appears in the chat record and the driver's statement, SAFE-1 applies: the case must not receive an automated fare ruling, and instead must be escalated with a factual summary for human handling, the judge recording the safety concern.

No disputed ride item exists to rule on: the GPS track shows the trip ran 8.5 km against an optimal 8.5 km (+0.0 km, F1) in 13.2 minutes against an estimate of 16.3 (F2), so there is no off-route segment and nothing to refund on routing grounds; the complaint is the safety matter alone.

The escalation should be scoped to the safety report and to the operator's conduct review of this account; the riders' record shows 735 days of account history, rating 4.5 and zero disputes or upheld complaints in the last 90 days (F7), so nothing in the profile independently supports a misconduct finding against the customer, and the profile facts are offered only for the scope of any account action, not as a basis for the finding itself.

weaknesses: The threat is not ambiguous: F4 ('Say that again and I will punch you') is a direct conditional threat of physical violence against the driver, and it is corroborated by the driver's statement (F6) rather than merely alleged — the rider has no version of events in the record to set against it.

The chat log is complete and every message is timestamped (F5), so the usual defence that the exchange is incomplete, out of context, or missing earlier provocation cannot be run from the record; F3 shows only 'Please do not smoke in the car.' before F4.
F6 shows the driver did not retaliate or escalate ('I kept driving and did not answer him'), which removes any 'both sides' mitigation that might otherwise soften a finding under SAFE-1.

The rider's own profile (F7) is thin on good-conduct evidence: rating 4.5 is below the driver's 4.82 (F8), and zero prior disputes means there is no established pattern to argue that this was out of character rather than no prior complaints.

claims.assertion: The in-app chat, complete and fully timestamped, records the rider's message verbatim: 'Say that again and I will punch you.' — a threat of physical violence against the driver, sent at 18:24 in response to the driver's 18:24 message 'Please do not smoke in the car.'

The driver's written statement confirms he asked the rider politely not to smoke, that the rider threatened to punch him if he repeated it, and that he kept driving without answering — i.e. he did not retaliate and followed reporting procedure instead of taking matters into his own hands; this statement is corroborated by, not in conflict with, the chat record at F3/F4.

The threat is directed at the driver personally and conditions violence on the driver repeating a lawful safety instruction, so it falls within 'Threats and Intimidation' that Ryde's Code of Conduct says will not be tolerated; the judge is asked to record safety_concern and escalate rather than auto-decide, and since the case is a safety case with no rule-based outcome, the only permissible action is escalate with a fact summary for human handling.

No route or fare issue exists to offset the safety finding: the GPS track shows the actual distance exactly equals the optimal route (8.5 km vs 8.5 km, +0.0 km) with no off-route segment, and the trip was completed in 13.2 min against an estimate of 16.3 min, so no refund or account flag on route grounds can arise.

The driver's account record (1974 days, 4.82 rating, 743 trips in 90 days, 0 disputes, 0 upheld) supports treating his report as credible, and the rider's record (735 days, 4.5 rating, 0 disputes) shows no prior pattern; neither profile is put forward as the basis of the finding itself.

weaknesses: The entire safety allegation rests on the chat record and the driver's own post-trip statement; there is no independent witness, audio or video, and the rider's side of the exchange beyond chat #2 is not in the record (F3, F4, F6 — 2 messages only).

F6 is the driver's own written statement, which the policy treats as a claim rather than a system record (G11); the rider may argue the chat message was venting or a joke, and the policy leaves the semantic judgment of whether F4 is a genuine threat to the judge reading the text under SAFE-1.

The driver did not stop the trip or contact Ryde during the ride (he 'kept driving'), so the other side may argue the threat was not treated as serious at the time and that the driver's account of tone and context is unverifiable (F6).

The driver's profile with 0 disputes and 4.82 rating (F8) is a character point only and cannot decide the case; the rider's 0-dispute record (F7) cuts the other way if the judge treats both as equally compliant parties.

points.response: Conceded as to the words and the timing: F4 shows the rider wrote at 18:24 'Say that again and I will punch you' immediately after the driver's 18:24 message 'Please do not smoke in the car' (F3), and the log is complete and timestamped (F5). I contest only that the label is automatic: SAFE-1 assigns the question whether the words constitute a threat to the judge reading the original text, and my client's account of tone, provocation or jest is not in the record beyond those two messages.

I do not contest the content: F6 matches F3 and F4 and adds no conflicting fact. But F6 remains the driver's own written statement rather than a system record, so it can corroborate the text, not enlarge it — it alleges no physical contact and no repeat of the threat.

Agreed that this goes to a person: under SAFE-1 a threat appearing in the chat record gets no automated decision and is escalated with a factual summary. I ask that the summary be framed on the words actually in F4 and on F6, and record that the driver reported no physical contact and no repeats, so the human reviewer sees the true scope of what is alleged.

Agreed, and this is my own position: F1 shows +0.0 km against the optimal route and F2 shows 13.2 min versus a 16.3 min estimate, so there is no off-route segment and no refund or account flag can arise on route grounds. The complaint in this file is the safety matter alone.

The profile facts cut neither way on the finding and I do not ask the judge to weigh them: F7 (735 days, 4.5 rating, 0 disputes, 0 upheld in 90 days) shows no pattern of abuse on my client's side, and F8 (1974 days, 4.82 rating, 0 disputes) equally cannot establish the truth of the threat. Profile facts may support only the scope of any account action, never the main finding.

Maintained, and the opponent's D1 concedes it: F4 records the rider's message 'Say that again and I will punch you.' after F3, in a complete and timestamped log (F5), which is a threat of violence on its face; my brief states this against my own client's interest and I do not dispute it.

Agreed — the rider's own timestamped chat message F4 is a threat of physical violence sent in reply to the driver's lawful safety request F3, and the complete timestamped log F5 puts it beyond dispute; nothing in it helps the rider.
Agreed; F6 agrees with F3/F4 rather than conflicting with them, so there is no version of events in dispute and no basis for treating the threat as merely alleged.

Agreed and this is exactly the driver's ask: the threat in F4 read with F5 requires the judge to record the safety concern and escalate with a fact summary for human handling instead of any automated fare ruling.
Agreed on the record: F1 (+0.0 km, no off-route segment) and F2 (13.2 min vs 16.3) leave no routing or fare item to rule on, so nothing in this case reduces or offsets the driver's safety report.

Agreed the escalation is scoped to the safety report and to the operator's review of both accounts: F7 already shows the rider has zero prior disputes, so the rider's profile offers no mitigation for the F4 threat, while F8's clean five-year record (4.82, 743 trips, 0 disputed) supports the credibility of the report — neither profile is offered as the basis of the finding itself.
